summary: This paper proves that deterministic convertibility rho -> sigma in quantum-state texture (QST) for any finite dimension D >= 2 requires no (D-1)^2-variable complex SDP, being completely characterized by the one-parameter scalar resolvent family c_lambda(rho) = p - x^dagger(R + lambda I_{D-1})^{-1}x (and equivalently ||sigma - t f_1||_1 <= ||rho - t f_1||_1 for all t >= 0). Via delta-regularized Slater duality and simultaneous congruence diagonalization, every separating witness decomposes into a free-population term plus at most D-1 resolvent evaluations, reducing decision to nonnegativity of a univariate polynomial of degree <= 2D-2. For rank-1-coherence states, a closed-form C^1-matched two-regime square-root boundary replaces de Leon's Fig. 3 SDP curves and yields a rational witness (-3/50 at lambda=3/20) for Eq. (64). A full-rank rational qutrit pair with a 4-Kraus channel proves strict advantage over spectral-measure Blackwell dominance (+21/1250 violation), complemented by a sharp Kraus-rank ceiling D on rank-<=1-remainder boundaries and exact dilution scaling.
strengths: Self-contained elementary linear-algebraic proof of Theorem 1 via delta-regularized Slater duality and simultaneous congruence diagonalization of (H_{1,delta}, M), yielding a sharp D-1 bound on finite resolvent evaluations in any separating witness.

Exact closed-form C^1-matched two-regime square-root boundary (Theorem 2) for rank-1-coherence states in arbitrary dimension D >= 2, solving de Leon's Fig. 3 curves analytically and giving the instant rational scalar obstruction c_{3/20}(sigma) - c_{3/20}(rho) = -3/50 on Eq. (64).

Clean full-rank rational qutrit witness (Theorem 3(a)) with an explicit 4-Kraus QST channel (T = diag(1,0)) demonstrating a strict +21/1250 separation beyond classical spectral-measure Blackwell dominance.

Strong multi-layer verification: 18 constructive Lean 4.35.0 theorems (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice, 0 custom axioms), 16 AST-audited zero-float SHA-256 certificates, and 56 passing adversarial pytest checks including 75 CLARABEL SDP comparisons.
weaknesses: In main.tex, definition and remark share the theorem counter, so Theorems 1, 2, and 3 (as named in section titles, abstract, and Table 1) render in the compiled PDF as Theorem 2, Theorem 4, and Theorem 5.

Theorem 3(b) states minimal Kraus rank 1 + r_T max(1, r_Delta) for 'the normal-form channel of de Leon's Theorem 2'; as the proof shows, this applies to the measure-and-prepare residual construction Phi(Z) = Tr[(I - T^dagger T)Z] omega rather than arbitrary CP completions Phi (for example, T = 0 with Phi(Z) = Z oplus 0 can achieve smaller Kraus rank when r_T, r_Delta >= 2, though the r_Delta <= 1 ceiling D holds unconditionally).

The constructive Lean 4.35.0 suite formalizes the 18 cleared-denominator integer identities, rational witnesses, and arithmetic bounds rather than the complex matrix analysis, Slater duality, and hyperplane separation steps of Theorem 1, which rely on pen-and-paper proof plus numerical SDP cross-checks.
strong_novelty_candidates: Complete characterization of finite-dimensional deterministic QST convertibility by the scalar resolvent family c_lambda(rho) with at most D-1 dual resolvent evaluations per strictly separating witness and degree <= 2D-2 univariate polynomial reduction.
Closed-form C^1-matched two-regime boundary y_max(q, s_0) achieved by explicit rank-1 contractions T* for arbitrary-dimension rank-1-coherence states, replacing de Leon's Fig. 3 pointwise SDPs.
Purely rational full-rank qutrit separation proving that QST convertibility strictly outperforms classical spectral-measure Blackwell dominance.
